transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. We have a limit increase request on the table today. Our corporate counterparty currently has an approved derivatives exposure limit of $20 million and has requested an increase to $35 million. The derivatives desk expects this will support additional interest-rate and foreign-exchange hedging activity. Following our normal process, I'd like to go around the table. Let's start with credit risk -- what's your assessment of the counterparty's credit profile and any concerns with the requested increase?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag something important before we proceed. I received the counterparty's updated rating assessment this morning. Under the bank's single-name limit matrix, the counterparty's current rating band permits a maximum derivatives exposure limit of exactly $28 million. This assessment has not yet been entered in the committee pack, so you wouldn't have seen it. This means the requested $35 million would exceed the maximum permitted under our limit matrix by $7 million, though it would allow a partial increase from the current $20 million up to $28 million.

transcript.text: Before we finalize anything, I want to share relevant documentation information. I confirmed yesterday that the counterparty's newly signed credit-support annex permits daily variation-margin calls with a $250,000 minimum transfer amount. However, the executed annex is still awaiting upload to the legal repository, so it's not yet visible in our systems.

I confirmed with the counterparty's treasury team this afternoon that they will post exactly $4 million in cash collateral before the increased limit is activated. This confirmation is in the desk's email folder and has not yet been added to the exposure request documentation the committee has been reviewing.
